title: Jason Cohen on the growth ceiling, weaknesses as strategy, and adopting AI with urgency not chaos
summary: Jason Cohen explains the growth-ceiling math (new customers per month divided by churn rate), argues a defensible strategy is a unique set of strengths and weaknesses that reinforce each other (WP Engine), and says to adopt AI with urgency but not chaos. He also covers ICP focus, craft lost to AI coding, and being your own advocate.

principles.text: Your growth ceiling is new customers per month divided by monthly cancellation rate; marketing doesn't scale with your size but churn does.
principles.quote: it's just this new customers per month divided by the cancellation rate.

principles.text: Show founders the hard cap on customers to reframe churn; it sidesteps arguing about whether a given rate is acceptable.
principles.quote: instead of arguing about that, which is so abstract, it's much better to say you're never going to have more than 2,000 customers. You good with that?

principles.text: Strategy is a unique set of strengths and weaknesses where the weaknesses enable the strengths; competitors can copy strengths but not your trade-offs.
principles.quote: the important thing is that those weaknesses are feeding enabling the strengths not just weak right and then you have a special set to me that's a strategy

principles.text: Nothing was ever uncopyable on code; competitors could copy you but it doesn't fit their business model, so they won't.
principles.quote: it's not that nobody could copy it. They could, but it doesn't make sense for them in their set of trade-offs to do so.

principles.text: Adopt AI with urgency but not chaos: learn the mindset (skills, agents) rather than chasing one tool, or you fall behind.
principles.quote: you should be getting into AI not because this is how it's going to be from now on. It's not but because if you don't start now then when and how far behind will you be?

principles.text: Build everything for one specific ideal customer; a wider swath will still buy, but the bullseye gives focus and clear decisions.
principles.quote: Nevertheless, that's your north star. That's your vision. That's your strategy. That's what you're working for. It's focus.
